displayText: Here's the curve y equals e to the x. Squash it sideways, and you get y equals e to the two x. Or slide it one unit left, and you get y equals e to the x plus one. At x equals zero, which new curve do you think is steeper? Hold on to your guess. Here's the twist. Only one of them puts a new factor into its derivative, and it might not be the one you'd pick. By the end, you'll know why, and how to differentiate k e to the a x plus b.
